'''''Pancotto''''' is an [[Italian cuisine|Italian]] [[soup]] prepared with pieces of [[stale bread]] boiled in [[broth]] or water and seasoned.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Lorena Fiorini|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=AZXr0sjWy0UC&dq=Pancotto&pg=PT145|title=Il grande libro del pane|publisher=Newton Compton Editori|year=2012|isbn=978-88-541-4401-9}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Pancotto in Vocabolario|url=http://www.treccani.it/vocabolario/pancotto/|website=treccani.it}}</ref>

It is a dish from the cuisine of recovery that recalls [[peasant]] culture that would not waste bread, present in all [[regions of Italy]] with many variations due to the type of bread, the liquid used, and the cooking process. As a consequence, it has many names, such as [[Lombard cuisine|Lombard]] panada, [[Cuisine of Liguria|Ligurian]] ''pancheuto'', and [[Cuisine of Sardinia|Sardinian]] ''pane cottu''.

In the past, especially in [[Lombardy]] and [[Tuscany]], it was used to promote [[lactation]] and it was served to convalescents.
